summary: E-library fixes. LIVE BLOCKER, root cause found. Playing an http Network item did not crash because of a .help tooltip on a freed responder. The real cause: every dismiss, postAction and postLogin of an engine dialog raised an NSInvalidArgumentException inside a MainActor task. VLCDialogBackend sent the dialog id as a String, and -[MXRDialogServices performCommand:] calls unsignedLongLongValue on it, which NSString does not implement. The unified log at 08:52:08 shows the exception, thrown from -[MXRDialogServices performCommand:arguments:error:] ← VLCDialogBackend.dismiss ← MXRNativePresentations.refresh. AppKit swallowed it; the crash report notes "SOME_OTHER_THREAD_SWALLOWED_AT_LEAST_ONE_EXCEPTION". The unwind left Swift's executor tracking pointing at a dead frame. The next MainActor.assumeIsolated, here from the tooltip timer's hit-test, crashed reading identity 0x1e. Fixed on both sides: Swift now sends NSNumber, and the bridge reads the id by type, so a bad id gives an NSError, never an exception. A headless engine probe and a Swift regression test both fail without the fix. Also fixed: the Light mini-player over-video controls (S46 major), the mini player scaling with the window, the breadcrumb dropping the current folder, '1 items' counts, Add File inside a playlist, D039 (Add Audio Tracks disabled for songs), the S35 and S40 fixtures, and the grid-card selection fill. Convert/Stream no longer record watch state: the output playlist is now parented to the interface, and an engine probe proved the rule. Arrow keys: D-menus did the routing part in parallel (libraryListHasKeyboardFocus, set in MXRLibraryView), and I kept it. The view-level test with real key events could not be built. SwiftUI focus and gestures do not respond to synthetic NSEvents in a window that is never ordered on screen; I tried 6 ways (listed in notFixed).
fixed: LIVE BLOCKER http Network play crash: root cause is a dialog-id type mismatch (String vs NSNumber), which raised an ObjC exception inside a MainActor task, which corrupted Swift executor tracking, which then crashed the TooltipBridge hit-test in MainActor.assumeIsolated. Fixed in VLCServiceBackends.swift (NSNumber ids) and MXRDialogServices.m (id read by type, no exception). Evidence: `log show` 08:52:08 NSInvalidArgumentException backtrace; probe ../build/evidence/final6/fix/E-library/crash/probe-output.txt (before: 'string id: EXCEPTION NSInvalidArgumentException' FAIL; after: PASS); Swift test DialogBridgeArgumentTests fails without the fix (revert-check.txt).

notesForOthers: C-bridge: any ObjC exception in a bridge call made from a Swift task (MXRServicesBridge performCommand/request) is swallowed by AppKit. It corrupts Swift executor tracking and later crashes far away in MainActor.assumeIsolated (the TooltipBridge stack). Consider wrapping -[MXRServicesBridge performCommand:service:arguments:error:] in @try/@catch that converts the exception to an NSError, so this class of bug fails loudly at its source. J-media-io: MXRMediaServices.m output playlist is now vlc_playlist_New(VLC_OBJECT(intf), …) (one line, see the comment). It does not touch your extension-signature edits. Note that the tone playlist in MXRAudioServices.m is still instance-parented, which only matters if it ever plays an ML file. G-panels: the library drag payload is an NSURL (one row) or newline-separated URL text (several rows); your QueueListDropDelegate (.url/.plainText) accepts both. The queue-replace symptom is drop-target priority over the window open-and-play drop. D-menus: you edited MXRLibraryView (libraryListHasKeyboardFocus). I kept it and removed my duplicate view test (synthetic focus does not work offscreen). A-window: the S72 D051 deviation is still yours. Integrator: the test target was intermittently broken by other areas (QueueDropLiveFindingsTests MediaItem.url, WindowLiveRun2Tests CGSize Hashable on macOS 14, PlayerView ContinueButtonStyle). My suites were verified in an isolated copy.
